html:
Luís de Camões was the greatest poet of Portugal, author of The Lusiads, the national epic, published in 1572.

He lived the life of the empire he wrote about. He lost an eye fighting in North Africa, was jailed after a street fight in Lisbon and spent about seventeen years in Asia as a soldier and official. By tradition he survived a shipwreck in the Mekong delta by swimming ashore holding his manuscript.

The Lusiads tells the voyage of Vasco da Gama to India in ten cantos, as the story of the whole Portuguese people, with the gods of Olympus taking sides. He also wrote fine love poems. He died poor in Lisbon. The day of his death, 10 June, is the national day of Portugal, and his tomb is in the Jerónimos Monastery.
sum: Luís de Camões was the greatest poet of Portugal, author of The Lusiads, the national epic, published in 1572.
